raw_response:
I farm by starting from what worked for me last year, then I only change a little. I am not on big land, only 6 mu, so every bag of fertilizer is money, but I still do not dare save too hard on fertilizer because if yield drops, that loss is bigger than wasting a little input. In Quzhou our wheat-maize land can still give steady output with water from the well, so I will keep 4 mu in the wheat-maize rotation and leave 2 mu for cotton. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put the main fertilizer under before sowing, then topdress once at jointing, and water about 3 times if the season is normal. For summer maize after wheat, I will mostly follow what people around me do now: hybrid seed, enough nitrogen, one bottom dose and one chase dose, and 2 irrigations if rain is not enough. Cotton is slower and needs more watching, so on my 2 mu I will use improved seed, give it more potash than grain crops, and spray more times because insects are always the trouble there. I do not like making big risky changes at my age, so I will stay close to the usual local way, with enough fertilizer, enough water, and timely spraying, aiming for a steady harvest more than gambling on saving a few yuan.
